quizName: Hardest Questions in Montana Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: How can you help others see you while riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright colors. Always use your headlight and turn signals.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out and hit you.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out and hit you.
questions.explanation: Parked cars are dangerous because drivers may pull out without looking. Car doors can open into your lane, and people may step out between cars.

questions.question: How should a helmet fit to give you the best protection?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards. It must fit snugly all the way around and have no damage.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend who has been drinking wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. It helps to ask other friends to apply peer pressure.

questions.question: Which helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: One that meets U.S. DOT standards.
One that has survived a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all around your head.

questions.question: What happens when you take corners too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will usually stay in your lane.
It is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before turning.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle fit you properly?

options.text: When you can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
When you can reach the controls by stretching.
When the handlebars go over your head.
When your feet cannot reach the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should easily reach and use all the controls.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to go faster.
Only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Why are mirror checks important?

options.text: You should only check them on long trips.
They should be part of your regular checking routine.
They are not helpful because you cannot do anything about traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be part of your regular checking routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while riding. Always check them before changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: When you ride, the best gear to wear is:

options.text: Any gear that helps protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Use a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your BAC (blood alcohol content). Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: Your main source of information about your motorcycle should be:
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is your best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes specifications, how to operate it, and maintenance tips.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the single most important action you can take to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Which one is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves. A stocking cap is not protective gear.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates have poor traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface for motorcycles.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is enough.
Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire can look fine even if it is under-inflated, so you cannot rely on looking at it.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can be more visible by:
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you in one area of the lane with limited movement.
Lets you rely on others to spot hazards.
Requires you to go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: To get the best protection, make sure your helmet:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding. It protects you in a crash and helps prevent dehydration in warm weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for riders.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: When riding, wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.
